deal_summary: The customer explored automating filling, capping, and labeling of 5 L and 10 L canisters, then specified two prepared solutions that must not be mixed (e0, e3-e4). The seller developed a custom two-product configuration and the customer remained technically interested, but internal review by the general director and operations stakeholders took time (e5-e13). In the final direct call, the customer said the proposal was interesting but not financially approved because funds were allocated to another project, with possible reconsideration months later (e14).

customer_need.summary: Automate filling 5 L and 10 L canisters with screw caps and a side label; the initial manager worklog gives a 500/hour target for 5 L. The customer later specified two separate prepared liquids, buffered formalin and isopropyl alcohol, which must not be mixed. Technical details for different caps and the custom two-product configuration were clarified during the process (e0, e3-e4, e6, e8).

deal_dynamics.early: A date-only manager worklog says the customer was manually filling, wanted equipment soon enough to install within six months, and initially considered a price from 4 million acceptable (e0). The seller requested exact cap and label information; the customer waited for cap drawings and then sent dimensions (e1-e3).
deal_dynamics.middle: The customer specified two distinct solutions in batches of about 2,000 L and said mixing was not allowed. The seller developed an updated two-product line, and manager worklogs describe further production calculations and a quote range of 6-8 million. The customer continued to discuss the technical configuration and its pump (e4-e8).
deal_dynamics.late: The customer described a staged approval process led by the general director, followed by production and facilities review. The seller sent a one-page proposal and offered a short online engineering meeting. The final direct call says the proposal remained interesting but finance was not approved because funds went to another project; the customer estimated a later review in about three months or closer to winter (e9-e14).

positive_signals: The customer provided cap measurements and detailed the two-product requirement, including that the solutions could not be mixed (e2-e4).
The customer engaged with the revised custom proposal, asked about the pump, and described production/staffing plans if the project proceeded (e6, e8-e9).
The customer directly said the proposal remained interesting and that no technical questions were then outstanding, while explaining the funding constraint (e14).
negative_signals: The customer's general director did not review or decide on the proposal for several weeks, according to the customer's calls (e9-e10, e12).
The customer said the available money was allocated to another project, moving any possible review out by several months (e14).
customer_behavior.initiative: The customer supplied missing package data, clarified the solution composition and separation requirement, asked detailed questions about the custom equipment, and explained its decision process and funding position (e2-e4, e8-e10, e14).
customer_behavior.decision_process: The customer described a staged internal review: the director first reviews the proposal, then production and facilities/utility stakeholders discuss installation requirements, followed by a broader supplier discussion. The customer said the director's availability delayed the initial review and later said funds were allocated elsewhere (e10, e12, e14).

strong_actions: The seller requested exact container/cap information and forwarded the customer's product details for technical review (e1-e4).
The seller sent a revised proposal for two separate products with a supporting line video, then discussed the pump and custom configuration with the customer (e6, e8).
The seller prepared a one-page management summary and offered a short online engineering call when director review was pending (e11).
weak_actions: The director's review remained the next step across repeated check-ins; the record does not show a firm director meeting date or an alternate approval route before the final budget deferral (e9-e13).

The custom quotation depended on additional supplier/production calculations. Some of that timing is described only in date-only manager worklogs, so exact elapsed time and individual responsibility are uncertain (e5, e7).
manager_behavior.follow_up_quality: The seller continued follow-up, collected technical information, revised the custom offer, and provided executive-facing material. However, the sequence remained dependent on a customer-side director review that was repeatedly delayed, and no meeting with the director is recorded before the funding update (e5-e13).
manager_behavior.next_step_control: The seller arranged check-ins around expected internal meetings and offered a video conference, but the customer could not predict when the director would review the proposal. The last direct exchange established a possible future review window rather than an immediate next step (e10-e14).

turning_points.description: The customer specified two prepared liquids and stated that mixing them was not allowed, requiring a separated two-product configuration.
The seller sent an updated proposal for filling two different products; the customer continued technical review of the custom configuration.
The customer described the required director-first review and the later production/facilities review, making internal approval timing a visible dependency.
The customer said finance was not approved because funds had gone to another project, and estimated a later review several months away.

primary_trajectory_explanation.category: Internal budget priority and approval timing
primary_trajectory_explanation.explanation: The seller and customer developed a technically relevant custom configuration, and the customer explicitly said the proposal remained interesting. The clearest late-stage constraint is the customer's account that the general director had not prioritized the review and that funds were ultimately allocated to another project. The final call points to a later budget window rather than a technical rejection (e5, e7, e9-e14). This describes the observed trajectory and does not predict a later decision.

secondary_factors: The two liquids could not be mixed, so the offer required a custom separated-product setup (e4, e6, e8).

Date-only manager worklogs describe an initial price from 4 million as acceptable and later proposals in a 6-8 million range; the customer's final direct explanation was that funds went to another project, not that it rejected a stated price (e0, e7, e14).
The customer required cap drawings and exact product composition before the custom equipment could be finalized (e1-e4).

what_could_be_done: When director review first begins slipping, ask the customer to schedule a short technical and financial review with the director and operations stakeholders, using the one-page summary already prepared (e9-e13).
Reconfirm budget availability, approval timing, and the customer's future purchase window before continuing supplier-specific quotation work (e7, e10, e14).
Keep the two-product separation, cap sizes, pump requirements, and installation assumptions in a customer-approved specification sheet for any later review (e3-e8, e10).
limits: The customer said the director controlled the review timing and that funds were committed to a different project (e10, e12, e14).
Production and facilities stakeholders were expected to assess installation only after the director's initial review (e10).
The custom configuration required supplier/production input, and some status about that work appears only in manager worklogs (e5, e7).

evidence.paraphrase: Date-only manager worklog (time/year inferred): describes manual filling, 5 L and 10 L canisters with screw caps, a side label, a 500/hour target for 5 L, a six-month installation goal, and initial price comfort around 4 million. This is a manager claim.
Seller asks for the exact diameter and height of the caps for the technical calculation.
Customer says it requested cap drawings from the manufacturer and is waiting for them; seller says those dimensions are the remaining information needed for the proposal.
Customer supplies a 50.2 mm diameter and 21.3 mm height for the 5 L cap and an attached drawing for the 10 L cap.
Customer describes two planned solutions, buffered 10% formalin and isopropyl alcohol, prepared in advance in large batches, and says they must not be mixed.

Date-only manager worklog (time inferred): says the customer liked the proposal technically and on price, was collecting offers through August, and planned to decide on autumn purchasing; it also lists further dosage, label-height, and printer changes. This is a manager claim.
Seller sends an updated quotation for filling two different products and includes a line video.

Date-only manager worklog (time inferred): reports several proposals in the 6-8 million range and says this offer was technically attractive because it would not require washing the equipment. This is a manager claim.
Customer discusses the custom two-product filling setup and asks whether the membrane pump is pneumatic or electric, citing the alcohol product; seller agrees to clarify.
Customer says the director has not responded to any of the proposals, but the customer is interested and wants to plan staffing and future production.

Customer explains that the director must review first; production and facilities/utility representatives would then discuss installation conditions before a broader supplier meeting. Timing depends on the director's availability.
Seller sends a one-page summary for the management meeting and offers a 15-minute engineering call for the director.
Customer says the director has seen the offer but has not had time to review it or give a decision; the parties defer another check-in by about a week.
Seller asks whether the director has questions about the two-product separation, pump, or communications and offers to collect them for a video meeting.

Customer says the proposal is technically interesting but was not financially approved because the money was allocated to another project; the customer estimates reconsideration in at least about three months, possibly closer to December.

uncertainties: Initial price comfort, six-month installation goal, and intermediate proposal status are date-only manager claims rather than direct customer statements (e0, e5, e7).

The final price and equipment specification may have changed as the custom two-product design evolved; the customer's final direct explanation was that funds were redirected rather than a specific price objection (e5-e8, e14).
The manager cannot be shown to have controlled the director's review schedule or internal allocation of funds; the customer described these as internal decisions (e10, e12, e14).
The view ends before the customer's stated possible future review window, so no later decision is established (e14).
